case_name: Shane Roy Needham v. Janet Lea Needham

issues.label: Standard of review on second appeal
issues.why: The Supreme Court must determine whether it reviews the magistrate directly or the district court's intermediate appellate decision.

issues.label: Abuse of discretion in property division
issues.why: The court must assess whether the magistrate properly exercised discretion under the four-part abuse-of-discretion standard.

issues.label: Failure to value the shares
issues.why: Whether the magistrate erred by declining to determine fair market value before dividing community property.

issues.label: Proper valuation date for shares
issues.why: Whether shares should be valued as of divorce decree, trial, or another date affects equitable division.

issues.label: Natural enhancement of community asset
issues.why: Whether post-decree appreciation of the shares belongs to the community or one spouse.

issues.label: In-kind division versus monetary buyout
issues.why: Whether awarding shares in-kind rather than a monetary offset was an appropriate remedy.

issues.label: Substantial equality of division
issues.why: Idaho Code 32-712 presumes substantially equal division absent compelling reasons for inequality.

issues.label: Application of Josephson and Lamm precedent
issues.why: Whether closely-held corporation caselaw permits or forecloses simple in-kind stock division here.

issues.label: Impairment of share value by division
issues.why: Whether stripping majority control diminishes the value of Mr. Needham's remaining shares.

issues.label: Statutory factors under 32-712(1)(b)
issues.why: Whether the magistrate correctly weighed marriage duration, incomes, homemaker status, needs, and maintenance.

issues.label: Authority to compel BSA Waiver execution
issues.why: Whether the divorce court's equitable power permits ordering Mr. Needham to sign the waiver.

issues.label: Effect of Buy-Sell Agreement on transfer
issues.why: Whether a court-decreed transfer triggers the BSA's mandatory repurchase-at-book-value provision.

issues.label: BSA provision on involuntary/court-decree transfers
issues.why: Section 2(b) expressly covers transfers by court decree, potentially requiring repurchase.

issues.label: Whether Waiver alters the BSA
issues.why: Whether compelling the waiver improperly modifies a third-party contract without all parties' consent.

issues.label: Third-party rights of non-party shareholders
issues.why: Pearson and Woods's contractual rights under the BSA may be affected by the transfer.

issues.label: Corporation's contractual repurchase obligation
issues.why: The BSA imposes an obligation on Alturas to purchase transferred shares, implicating a non-party.

issues.label: Ms. Needham's waiver of BSA rights
issues.why: Whether her signed acknowledgment binds her and affects her ability to receive shares outside the BSA.

issues.label: Disentanglement of the parties
issues.why: Whether the in-kind award actually separates the parties or leaves them entangled as co-shareholders.

issues.label: Justification for favoring one party's proposal
issues.why: Whether reliance on Alturas succeeding 'without Mr. Needham' was a permissible basis for the award.

issues.label: Deadlock-breaking rationale's propriety
issues.why: Whether using property division to resolve corporate governance deadlock is a legitimate consideration.

issues.label: Consideration of dividend income history
issues.why: Whether reliance on prior dividend usage to fund lifestyle was proper given no maintenance awarded.

issues.label: Attorney fees below for frivolous appeal
issues.why: Whether the district court properly awarded fees deeming the intermediate appeal frivolous.

issues.label: Attorney fees on appeal
issues.why: Whether either party is entitled to fees under applicable statutes for the current appeal.
